title: Maximize the Confusion of an Exam
summary: Given a string answerKey consisting of 'T' (true) and 'F' (false), and an integer k, determine the maximum number of consecutive 'T's or 'F's that can be achieved by changing at most k answers in the answerKey.
statement: Given a string answerKey consisting of 'T' (true) and 'F' (false), and an integer k, determine the maximum number of consecutive 'T's or 'F's that can be achieved by changing at most k answers in the answerKey. Each change involves setting any character in the answerKey to either 'T' or 'F'.
constraints: answer_key has 1 through 50000 T/F characters and 0 <= k <= len(answer_key).
Change at most k characters to maximize a consecutive run of one answer.
Return the greatest achievable run length.
hints: A target run is a window containing at most k occurrences of the opposite character.
Run the standard at-most-k sliding window once for target T and once for target F.
Expand right, count mismatches, shrink left while mismatches>k, and retain maximum width.
Every feasible window remains until a new character makes it infeasible; minimal shrinking preserves the widest feasible window ending at each right index.
editorial: Every feasible window remains until a new character makes it infeasible; minimal shrinking preserves the widest feasible window ending at each right index.

tests.explanation: Changing both F answers makes all four positions equal.
Changing either middle answer produces a run of three equal answers.
